objects.text: The plaster here is newer than the wall, and worse.^Somebody bricked up a doorway from the far side, in a hurry, and plastered what he could reach.
A stool, down here in the dark, facing the flour.^Somebody sits and guards it. From the look of the flour, he sleeps on duty.

objects.say: A board in the floor behind the counter lifts.^It was bolted from underneath. Now it is not.

objects.text: Kesh's tallies. One tablet for every pot he has ever sold, and three for every pot he has not.^The last one says: DOOR. BRICK. TOMORROW.
A stool, exactly on the line.^It belongs to both of them. Neither has sat on it in nine years, in case.

objects.say: Two planks, in iron hooks. They lift out.^Whoever barred this door did it from in here, and then left by the roof. Nobody in Ashkel does that but the cats, and one other.

objects.text: A cushion, in the exact middle of the mat, with a dent in it the shape of something that sleeps standing up.^It is still warm.
A whole shelf, labelled: GOAT, THE. GRAZING FEES OWED.^Eleven years of tablets. The oldest ones have been chewed.
One shelf is empty but for a label: GOAT, THE. PAID.^It has never held anything.
Her answers, written down before the questions.^The last one reads: {t}yes, but not the way you are hoping.{/}| It is not dated. They never are.
